title: Be an island
hook: to Ananda: be islands to yourselves, a refuge to yourselves, the dhamma your refuge (DN 16)

segments.voice: Yesterday: eighty years. The Buddha called his body an old cart held together with straps. Your line: the old cart still rolls.

A waiting room, a phone that won't ring, and one question underneath everything: what happens to us without them? Ananda sits in the shade beside the Buddha, who has just come through a serious illness. Ananda has been his attendant for many years. While the teacher lay sick, he admits, he held on to one comfort: surely the teacher would not pass away without leaving some last instruction for the community. Some plan. Someone in charge. The Buddha's answer isn't the one Ananda was hoping for. It hands the question straight back to him.
screen: `WHAT HAPPENS WITHOUT THEM?` → `ANANDA WANTS A PLAN.` → `NOT THE ANSWER HE HOPED FOR.`

segments.voice: First, the Buddha says, what does the community expect of me? I've taught everything, with nothing held back. There's no closed fist of a teacher here, no secret saved for the favorites. And I've never thought of myself as the one who must lead the community. So why would I leave a leader? Then comes the line. The key Pali word is dipa, and it has two meanings: an island, and a lamp. Translators have gone both ways. In 1881 T. W. Rhys Davids rendered it with lamps: "be ye lamps unto yourselves. Be ye a refuge to yourselves." Other translators hear island: be an island to yourself, a refuge to yourself, with the dhamma as your island, the dhamma as your refuge, and no other. An island is solid ground when the flood is rising all around. A lamp is light when everyone else's has gone out. Either way, the point is the same. Don't lean your whole weight on a person, even me. Stand on what you've seen for yourself, and on the teaching itself. How? The Buddha answers right there: by practicing mindfulness, watching the body, feelings, the mind and the way things are, steadily, with clear attention. The island isn't stubbornness, and it isn't going it alone. It's having practiced enough that when the waters rise, there's ground under your feet. A teacher who refuses to name a successor tells his students to be their own light, and their own ground.
screen: `NO CLOSED FIST, NOTHING HELD BACK.` · `DIPA: AN ISLAND, OR A LAMP.` · `THE DHAMMA AS YOUR REFUGE.` · `THE ISLAND IS BUILT BY PRACTICE.` · then, large: `BE YOUR OWN ISLAND.`

segments.voice: Feel the ground under you, the chair, the floor, the steadiness of it: that's your island for now. Think of one small decision you've been waiting for someone else to make, what to eat, whether to call, which way to go, and ask yourself what you actually see and know. Let the answer come from your own ground.
Dipa. Island, and also lamp: the Buddha's answer to Ananda, be a dipa and a refuge to yourselves, with the dhamma your refuge.
Your line: be your own island. Or, as Rhys Davids heard it, your own lamp. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Buddhist teachers often quote 'be an island to yourself' (or 'be a lamp') to encourage self-reliance grounded in practice, and the four foundations of mindfulness that the Buddha names here are still taught as a meditation practice.

fork.setup: you're the Buddha. Ananda is frightened and hopes you'll leave instructions and someone in charge. what do you tell him?
options: name your most trusted disciple as leader.
tell him to be an island to himself, with the dhamma as refuge.

fork.reveal: no successor. be an island, a refuge to yourselves, the dhamma your refuge, and build that island by practicing mindfulness.

original.note: Pali: island, and also lamp. Sanskrit keeps them apart: dvīpa (island), dīpa (lamp).

trapdoor: what you thought: go it alone, trust nobody.
what it means: don't lean your whole weight on any person; stand on what you've practiced and seen, with the dhamma as refuge.
what a scholar hears: DN 16, 2.26: attadipa viharatha attasarana anaññasarana; Pali dipa merges Sanskrit dvipa (island) and dipa (lamp), so translators split between the two.

sources.quoted: be ye lamps unto yourselves. Be ye a refuge to yourselves.

notes: Rhys Davids 1881 (SBE XI, The Book of the Great Decease, ch. 2 §33) quoted: 'be ye lamps unto yourselves. Be ye a refuge to yourselves.' Please check wording against the SBE text.
The 'closed fist' (acariya-mutthi) and 'I never thought I should lead the community' paraphrased from DN 16, 2.25.
Etymology note: Pali dipa covering both Sanskrit dvipa (island) and dipa (lamp); commentary reads 'island'. Confirm.
Original script given as दीप; confirm.
